notes.meaning: Peter writes a second letter to the believers he loves to keep their minds clear and focused on the truth. Even genuine Christians can easily forget what matters most. Peter knew that believers need gentle reminders to stay spiritually awake and faithful.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think a later writer used Peter's name. They point to the phrase "your apostles" as a clue. Others answer that this reads too much into the words.

notes.meaning: Believers are told to remember what God spoke through the Old Testament prophets and the commands Jesus gave through His apostles. Both groups spoke the exact same message about God's plan and His coming judgment. Holding firmly to these ancient scriptures protects Christians from being led astray.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think a later writer used Peter's name. They point to the phrase "your apostles" as a clue. Others answer that this reads too much into the words.

notes.meaning: Peter warns that in the final age before Christ's return, mockers will show up to make fun of Christian truth. These people do not argue fairly; they scoff because they only want to follow their own sinful desires. Their mockery should not shock believers, because the scriptures warned ahead of time that they would come.

differ.view: The "last days" are the whole time between Jesus' first coming and his return.
The "last days" are the days just before Christ comes back.

notes.meaning: The scoffers sneer and ask why Jesus has not returned yet, acting as if His promise has completely failed. They claim that the world has run smoothly without interruption ever since creation, so God will never step in. Because they do not want to face judgment, they pretend nothing will ever change.

Peter points out that these mockers deliberately ignore the history of creation. God formed the universe out of nothing simply by speaking His powerful word. The same God who ordered the waters to make the dry land has full authority over the physical world.

The scoffers also ignore the great flood in the days of Noah. The earth did not continue unbroken; God used the very waters of creation to wipe out an ungodly world. This ancient judgment proves that God does step into human history when wickedness overflows.

The present world is preserved by that same divine word, but it is stored up for fire instead of water. God is holding back the final destruction until the appointed day of judgment arrives. On that great day, ungodly people who rejected God will face total ruin.

Believers must not view time through human eyes, because God is eternal and does not age. To the Lord, a single day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years pass like a single day. What feels like an unbearable delay to people is only a brief moment in God's eternal plan.

God is not slow or late in keeping His word, as human beings often think. Instead, He is being remarkably patient with people so that they have time to turn away from their sins. He delays the final judgment because His desire is for people to find life through repentance, which means turning back to God.

differ.view: In Reformed theology, Peter is writing directly to the "elect"—the believers chosen by God. The delay of Christ's return ensures that not one of God's chosen people will be lost, but that every last one of them will be brought to repentance and saved.

In this tradition, God genuinely loves every human being and desires that no one be lost to judgment. He holds back the final day so that every person has a real chance to freely respond to His offer of mercy and choose life.

notes.meaning: The day of Christ's return will come suddenly and without warning, just like a thief breaking in at night. When that day arrives, the heavens will vanish with a rushing roar, and intense heat will melt the basic elements of the physical world. Everything on earth and all human works will be laid bare before God for judgment.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some of the oldest copies of this verse say the earth and its works "will be found" instead of "burned up." This is closer to the BSB's "laid bare." The exact wording here is hard to be sure of.

notes.meaning: Since the present world and everything in it will dissolve, believers ought to live very differently from the world around them. Knowing that earthly things are temporary should move Christians to live devoted, godly lives. Our focus belongs on eternal things rather than temporary earthly treasures.

Christians are called to look forward eagerly to the day of God and to help speed its arrival. Believers do this through earnest prayer, godly living, and sharing the good news with all nations. Even though that day brings fierce heat to melt the physical universe, believers await it with joy.

Relying on God's ancient promise, believers look forward to a brand-new heaven and earth. Unlike this present world that is full of sin and sorrow, this renewed home will be filled with pure goodness and justice. Those who trust in Christ will dwell there with Him in everlasting peace.

Because Christians have such a glorious hope, they should work hard to live at peace with God and others. Peter urges them to be found clean and without fault when Christ appears, clothed in His righteousness. Looking forward to Jesus should inspire believers to keep their hearts and daily lives pure.

Believers should view the Lord's patience not as neglect, but as an opportunity for more people to be saved. Peter mentions that their dear brother Paul wrote about these same truths with God-given wisdom. Even though the two apostles had differences in the past, Peter warmly honors Paul as a faithful partner in the gospel.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching has pointed to this verse to say that hard passages of Scripture should be understood with the guidance of the Church, not by each reader alone.

notes.meaning: Paul addressed the return of Christ and Christian living throughout his letters, though some of his explanations are difficult to grasp. People who lack spiritual understanding and stability twist Paul's words, just as they distort other parts of the Bible. Misusing God's word to justify sin leads to a person's own spiritual ruin.

notes.meaning: Since Christians have been warned ahead of time, they must stay alert and guard their faith. Peter cautions them not to be swept away by teachers who reject God's moral law. Staying watchful keeps believers from losing their firm footing in the truth.

differ.view: The warning is meant to shake us out of laziness, not to shake our trust in God's promises. The danger is drifting from firm truth into error, not losing God's grace.
True believers can never finally fall away from salvation. But they can lose their steadiness and begin to doubt and waver.
This is a real warning not to fall from the faith in Christ that brought us God's grace. Believers must keep holding on to God and his word.

notes.meaning: Instead of slipping backward, believers must keep growing in the undeserved favor and personal knowledge of Jesus Christ. True spiritual health requires ongoing growth in faith, love, and obedience. Peter closes his letter by giving all glory and honor to Jesus, both right now and forever.
